new_statements.rule_in_words: Lungchow (Longzhou) Zhuang is a six-tone language in which every syllable carries a tone; Li states that the dialect has no strong contrast between stressed and unstressed syllables, i.e. stress is not prominent and not distinctive, and that its stress patterns have not been studied. No position of word stress is given. (For the Po-ai dialect in the same book Li adds that final particles/enclitics are usually less stressed; that remark is not made for Lungchow.)
new_statements.exceptions: None stated for Lungchow; Li explicitly says no specific study of its stress patterns exists.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement about the dialect as a whole (word- and phrase-level stress together with intonation); based on Li's field data from the city of Lungchow (Longzhou), the eponymous variety of Zuojiang Zhuang. Access via Google Books full-text snippets of a copyrighted print book: two overlapping snippets give the complete sentence, but the page number is not visible.
new_statements.identity_note: The deciding statement is about Li Fang-Kuei's 'Lungchow' = the dialect of Longzhou city (龙州), the eponymous and representative variety of Zuojiang Zhuang (ISO 2006-128 lists 'Longzhou' and 'Nung Chao' as alternate names of zzj; Chinese sources call it 壮语南部方言左江土语, Glottolog has no separate languoid for the Longzhou dialect). Gedney/Hudak's Lungming (Longming, Tiandeng county) is also inside the zzj area per the ISO request. Note Pittayaporn 2009 finds Zuojiang not to be a single clade, and the Chinese Wikipedia lists Leiping 土话, Jinlong 岱话 and Longzhou as distinct sub-varieties; Li Shenglan 2022 describes the Jinlong 岱话 lect, not Longzhou city.

tone_statements.translation: 4. Tones. 1. Mid level, written 33; e.g. ja33 'medicine'. 2. Mid falling to low, a slow fall, written 31; e.g. ja31 'to cover; to mend'. 3. Half-low rising to half-high, written 24; e.g. ja24 'grass'. 4. Mid falling to low, a fast fall, always followed by glottal -ʔ, written 31 ... 5. High level, written 55; e.g. ja55 'finished'. 6. Low level (the end falls lower, like the Cantonese lower-even tone), written 11; e.g. ja11 'summer'. 7. High level (with final -p, -t, -k), long and short, long written 55:, short 55 ... 8. Half-low falling to low (with -p, -t, -k), likewise long and short, long written 21: ... 1-6 all end in a vowel or -m, -n, -ng and resemble the Chinese ping/shang/qu tones; 7-8 end in -p, -t, -k and resemble the Chinese entering tone.

tone.quote: 4. 聲調 1. 中平, 寫作 ˧ (33:); 例如 ja˧ 葯。 2. 中降至低, 是緩降調, 寫作 ˧˩ (31:); 例如 ja˧˩ 遮; 補。 3. 半低升至半高, 寫作 ˨˦ (24:); 例如 ja˨˦ 草。 4. 中降至低, 是速降調, 後面永遠有喉音-ʔ, 寫作 ˧˩ (31:) ... 5. 高平, 寫作 ˥ (55:); 例如 ja˥ 了。 6. 低平(尾更降低如廣州的陽平), 寫作 ˩ (11:); 例如 ja˩ 夏。 7. 高平(韵尾有-p, -t, -k), 有長短兩種, 長的寫作 ˥ (55:), 短促的寫作 ˥ (55) ... 8. 半低降至低(有-p, -t, -k), 亦有長短兩種, 長的寫作 ˨˩ (21:) ... 以上1—6都是元音或-m, -n, -ŋ收尾, 類似漢語的平上去三聲。 7—8都是有-p, -t, -k收尾的, 類似漢語的入聲。

tone.translation: 4. Tones. 1. Mid level, written 33; e.g. ja33 'medicine'. 2. Mid falling to low, a slow fall, written 31; e.g. ja31 'to cover; to mend'. 3. Half-low rising to half-high, written 24; e.g. ja24 'grass'. 4. Mid falling to low, a fast fall, always followed by glottal -ʔ, written 31 ... 5. High level, written 55; e.g. ja55 'finished'. 6. Low level (the end falls lower, like the Cantonese lower-even tone), written 11; e.g. ja11 'summer'. 7. High level (with final -p, -t, -k), long and short, long written 55:, short 55 ... 8. Half-low falling to low (with -p, -t, -k), likewise long and short, long written 21: ... 1-6 all end in a vowel or -m, -n, -ng and resemble the Chinese ping/shang/qu tones; 7-8 end in -p, -t, -k and resemble the Chinese entering tone.
tone.summary: Eight tone classes: mid level 33, slow fall 31, rising 24, fast fall 31 with final glottal stop, high 55, low 11 on smooth syllables; high 55 and low fall 21 (long/short) on -p -t -k syllables; no tone sandhi.
